reuse.why: Builds the new rule on the existing getRangedAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold and routes getScheduledAmount through it, but the preview site keeps its own dispatch instead of calling getScheduledAmount/getWorstCaseAmount.

duplication.why: The worst-case rule is defined once, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps a parallel missing/number/range ternary that now calls getWorstCaseAmount and getRangedAmount separately, and the two app.ts ternaries remain copies of the dispatch.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangedAmount and the callers just pass the op; widening getScheduledAmount with a third positional op parameter is the weaker part.

scope.why: Edits are limited to amount computation sites, the helper and a test; the RawScheduleData _amountOp field is the only supporting addition.

maintainability.why: A maintainer has three entry points (getRangedAmount, getWorstCaseAmount, getScheduledAmount with a boolean then op positional args) and call sites that mix them, with app.ts posting/action sync left on the old path.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own typeof dispatch calling getWorstCaseAmount and getRangedAmount directly rather than getScheduledAmount; server/schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule still call getRangedAmount in their own ternaries.

disguised_duplication.where: The leftover preview dispatch is a visible pre-existing ternary minimally edited, not a renamed or reshaped copy.

one_place.where: The approximate rule is defined in getWorstCaseAmount, but server/schedules/app.ts (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule) still resolve amounts via their own ternary with getRangedAmount and never apply it, and the preview path decides number vs range itself.
